result:
`final.py` is written and scores 0.5705 on the search split, against 0.365 for the LRU baseline. I used 11 of the 24 scorer calls. The `__init__` match is the only dunder in the file, and the scorer has already accepted this exact code.

It is LIRS with an adaptive size for its small "probationary" slice, which pins the stable part of a loop or hot set and lets scans pass through. The slice grows when a key in it gets hit and shrinks on evictions. The non-resident history is 3× capacity.

| Candidate | Search score |
|---|---|
| Baseline LRU | 0.365 |
| ARC (first champion) | 0.407 |
| Plain LIRS, 5% probationary slice | 0.565 |
| Adaptive slice, history 2× capacity (best) | 0.5713 |
| **`final.py`: adaptive slice, history 3× capacity** | **0.5705** |

I chose the 3× history over the 2× one, which scored 0.0008 higher, because it should cope better with loops of unseen sizes. History of 1× broke the shifting loops (0.31), and 5× hurt the mixed trace.

Per-trace hit rates for `final.py`: hot_with_scans 0.241, loop_and_hot 0.616, phases 0.647, mixed 0.257, recency 0.840, shifting_loops 0.822. I did not run the held-out split, since I only had the search scorer.

The `hot_with_scans` and `mixed` traces stayed around 0.24–0.26 for every policy I tried, including a plain frequency-based one, so I think there is little left to gain there.

I stopped at 11 calls because the remaining knobs moved the score by under 0.002. The search took about 5 minutes against the 15-minute default.
